summary: Incident evidence assembled; all causal explanations remain hypotheses.

actions.detail: Compare supporting and contradictory observations with the incident owner.

timeline.text: Lease-store request duration increased to 900 milliseconds; historical baseline was 20 milliseconds.
Consumers reported repeated lease acquisition timeouts.

hypotheses.explanation: A lease-store latency regression may have caused settlement consumers to time out while acquiring leases, reducing consumption and allowing the settlement queue to accumulate.

support.quote: Lease-store request duration increased to 900 milliseconds; historical baseline was 20 milliseconds.
Consumers reported repeated lease acquisition timeouts.

missing_checks: Whether lease-store latency increases align per-request with the lease acquisition timeout periods seen by settlement consumers.
Whether the lease acquisition timeout threshold is below or near the observed 900 millisecond lease-store request duration.
Whether settlement consumer throughput dropped during the same interval that queue depth increased.

hypotheses.explanation: Settlement consumers may have been unable to acquire leases because of lease coordination contention or failures, leading to queue growth; the lease-store latency increase could be related but is not sufficient alone to establish causation.

support.quote: Consumers reported repeated lease acquisition timeouts.
Lease-store request duration increased to 900 milliseconds; historical baseline was 20 milliseconds.

missing_checks: Whether multiple consumers were competing for the same leases or partitions during the incident window.
Whether lease acquisition failures occurred even for requests without elevated lease-store duration.
Whether lease-store error rates, lock contention, or retry counts increased alongside the reported timeouts.

hypotheses.explanation: The settlement backlog may reflect reduced settlement consumer progress, with repeated lease acquisition timeouts as the observable failure mode and elevated lease-store duration as a possible contributing symptom.

support.quote: Consumers reported repeated lease acquisition timeouts.
Lease-store request duration increased to 900 milliseconds; historical baseline was 20 milliseconds.

missing_checks: Whether settlement consumers were otherwise healthy, running, and processing messages during the queue growth.
Whether message ingress rate increased enough to explain a queue depth of 4200 messages without a consumer-side regression.
Whether other settlement dependencies besides lease-store showed latency or error changes in the same window.

unresolved_questions: No direct event text states the root cause of the lease-store latency increase.
No event text provides settlement consumer throughput, ingress rate, lease timeout configuration, or error-rate details.
